The variety of declinations from iron needles <term>obelis ferreis</term> <gloss>iron obelisks/needles</gloss> at various latitudes of the <term>terrella</term> <gloss>little earth/magnetic sphere</gloss>.

<note>A circular diagram represents a <term>terrella</term>, a small magnetic model of the Earth. An outer circle is labeled "Sphere of Virtue." Inside, a shaded sphere representing the <term>terrella</term> has a horizontal axis drawn through it. Along the circumference of this inner sphere, several small iron needles are depicted at various latitudes. At the equatorial points, the needles lie flat against the surface. As they move toward the top and bottom poles, they incline at increasingly steep angles, until they stand perfectly vertical at the magnetic poles.</note>

The declination of magnetic iron over the <term>terrella</term> is shown by various equal iron wires, of the length of a barleycorn, arranged upon the meridian. The wires at the equator are directed by the power of the stone toward the poles, and they lie upon the body parallel to its horizon. The closer they are placed to the poles, the more they are raised by a convertible nature: at the poles themselves, they tend perpendicularly toward the center. However, iron needles do not rise correctly unless on a vigorous stone, if they are longer than they ought to be.
